validated_results.title: MnSOD gene polymorphism association with steroid-dependent cancer.
validated_results.reason: The study evaluates the MnSOD Val16Ala genotype distribution in cancer cases and controls, providing no population-wide manganese nutritional exposure estimate.

validated_results.title: Glutathione peroxidase 1 (GPX1) genetic polymorphism, erythrocyte GPX activity, and prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: The reported risk estimate concerns the GPX1 Pro198Leu polymorphism and erythrocyte enzyme activity rather than a population-wide selenium exposure effect.

validated_results.title: Association of prostate cancer and manganese superoxide dismutase AA genotype influenced by presence of occult cancer in control group.
validated_results.reason: The analysis addresses the MnSOD AA genotype and control-group misclassification, with no nutritional manganese exposure estimate for prostate cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Dairy products, dietary calcium and vitamin D intake as risk factors for prostate cancer: a meta-analysis of 26,769 cases from 45 observational studies.
validated_results.reason: This is a meta-analysis pooling 45 observational studies rather than an original primary study of calcium and prostate cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Dairy products, dietary calcium and vitamin D intake as risk factors for prostate cancer: a meta-analysis of 26,769 cases from 45 observational studies.
validated_results.reason: The publication is a meta-analysis of observational studies on dairy intake and prostate cancer risk, not original human study data.

validated_results.title: Dairy products, dietary calcium and vitamin D intake as risk factors for prostate cancer: a meta-analysis of 26,769 cases from 45 observational studies.

validated_results.title: Orally administered isoflavones are present as glucuronides in the human prostate.
validated_results.reason: The study measures isoflavone glucuronide concentrations in prostate tissue and plasma of benign prostatic hyperplasia patients, providing mechanistic bioavailability data without any evidence on developing prostate cancer.
